messages.author: de0353bdfec15530
messages.subject: Immersive Interactive Heatmaps
parts:
Hi all,

I'm working on this Shiny app which creates an interactive heatmap and runs hierarchical clustering on the data, grouping similar rows and columns.  Specifically, I'm using the heatmap.2 function to generate the heatmap and dendrograms  What I'd like to be able to do, is that when the user clicks on a cell or a column or a row of the data, plots are generated for each of the selected cells using subject level data as opposed to group data (whether it be bar charts, violin plots, box plots, etc.).  Anyone have ideas/experience on how to implement such functionality?  Here are some things I've considered:

  1. Integrating InCHlib into my Shiny app (InCHlib: http://openscreen.cz/software/inchlib/home/)
  2. Allowing a user to drag a rectangle over the cells that they want to plot? 
  3. Creating a separate navbar page where you can enter tags for the x variable values and y variable values and generate plots accordingly (this is my backup plan; it's not as fancy or user friendly, but it would still work)

Thanks!

messages.author: b419b3f42893b2f1
messages.subject: Re: Immersive Interactive Heatmaps
parts:
Hi,

I've unsuccessfully tried to make clicking in heatmap.2 plots work to select rows/columns (clicking in other types of plots works very well as done in this wonderful example: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-testapp/blob/master/locator/server.r ). But maybe that's not what you're asking. 

A potential solution would be for the user to click "+/-" buttons to cycle through columns or rows in the heatmap and updating the other plots to represent what is currently "selected" (if you don't have many cols/rows this could be doable). The currently selected column could be highlighted using ColSideColors or RowSideColors in heatmap.2. 

As I said I've struggled a bit with this too... "Heatmap.3" is a modified version that allows for multiple color labels that you might want to check out if you haven't already.

Let me know if you figure out something smart!
Anders
